hypotheses.text: In the two families (Family T and Family K) described by Miyamoto et al. (2026), pyramidal tract involvement (mild gait spasticity) is present in more than 60 percent of adult affected carriers of RAB3A p.Arg83Trp but is incomplete in penetrance, manifesting as a variable co-phenotype rather than an obligate diagnostic criterion.
hypotheses.rationale: Miyamoto et al. state that affected individuals presented with adult-onset cerebellar symptoms 'often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors'. Testing the exact numerator and denominator breakdown across individual pedigree members of Family T and Family K will establish whether spasticity serves as a consistent core clinical discriminator or merely an optional sign in SCA52.

evidence.text: Miyamoto et al. reported two families with autosomal-dominant cerebellar ataxia harboring the heterozygous RAB3A p.(Arg83Trp) variant where affected individuals presented with adult-onset progressive cerebellar symptoms often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors.

source.title: An R83W mutation in Rab3A causes autosomal-dominant cerebellar ataxia
source.quote: In this study, we identified the c.247C > T p.(Arg83Trp) variant in RAB3A, encoding a small GTPase involved in membrane-associated regulated exocytosis, in two families with cerebellar ataxia. Affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms, often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors.

hypotheses.text: Action or postural tremor occurs in a substantial subset (between 50 percent and 80 percent) of affected individuals in Family T and Family K, reflecting dual cerebellar outflow and basal ganglia/synaptic disruption from RAB3A switch II dysfunction.
hypotheses.rationale: Tremor is highlighted in the primary description of autosomal dominant RAB3A-related ataxia alongside spasticity. Delineating its specific frequency across Family T and Family K will clarify if tremor can serve as an early clinical flag distinguishing SCA52 from pure cerebellar cortical degenerations such as SCA6.

evidence.text: Affected members harboring the p.(Arg83Trp) mutation exhibited adult-onset, gradually progressive ataxia accompanied by tremors and mild spastic gait.

hypotheses.text: Neurodevelopmental features, including cognitive delay or intellectual disability, exhibit lower penetrance (less than 40 percent) than adult cerebellar ataxia in heterozygous RAB3A p.Arg83Trp carriers, manifesting selectively or subclinically in Family T and Family K.
hypotheses.rationale: Miyamoto et al. qualify neurodevelopmental presentations as 'variable features of neurodevelopmental disorders' rather than invariant core signs. Testing whether intellectual disability is restricted to specific individuals or generations in Family T and Family K tests whether SCA52 is primarily a degenerative ataxia with variable neurodevelopmental expressivity.

evidence.text: The report highlights that neurodevelopmental features in patients with the heterozygous c.247C>T variant were variable rather than invariant.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient clinical tabular entries in the supplementary material of Miyamoto et al. (2026) for muscle tone, deep tendon reflexes, babinski sign, tremor classification, and formal IQ/neuropsychological scores across Family T and Family K?
new_directions.rationale: Direct examination of the supplementary clinical tables or main text pedigree tables will provide the exact integer numerators and denominators for spasticity, tremor, and intellectual disability needed to compute hard clinical frequencies.
